newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen building on two day rally.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen building on two day rally.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen extending recent gains on Tuesday with investors likley to again follow through despite a lack of change in economic fundamentals which will keep the bourse volatile in coming days, analysts said.
The SET Index soared 5.06 percent on Monday to 504.53. The SET 50 gained rose 2.41 points to 35.88 in heavy volumes as various technical factors and buying through mutual funds.
"I suspect we will see one of two days of drifting around, up and down, and certainly they'll keep it above five hundred," said Philip Adkins, head of research at Nava SC.
The second largest single day point decline in the Dow following damaging remarks by Japanese Prime Minister Hashimoto was unlikely to affect a Thai market fixed on domestic issues, analysts said.
"I don't think this is going to do much to the Thai market. It's not just decoupled from New York it's decoupled from the planet...," said one senior foreign analyst.
Some evidence of the government action to resolve the current economic crisis was needed to fundamentally change sentiment, Adkins said.
Allowing market mechanisms to effectively weed out some financially weak companies would also send a healthy signal to equity investors, he said.
The market was not expecting anything concrete from today's cabinet meeting said to be to discuss decrees to shore up the ailing finance and property sectors, analysts said.
If foreign funds were responsible for gains over the last two trading days the focus will again be on bluechip bank and telecommunications issues, analysts said.
Economic data from the central bank on Thursday and submission of the government budget to parliament on Wednesday may increase the incentive to take profits, analysts said.
